name: sed
smoke:
printf 'a
b
' | sed 's/a/X/' -> expect 'X
b'
blocker: GNU sed is structurally a gnulib program: 100 gnulib .c files in lib/ each #include config.h, a 2575-line header with 612 autoconf-probed HAVE_/GNULIB_/_GL_ macros produced by a ./configure run that probes the target libc. gnulib's entire purpose is configure-detected libc replacements; a wrong/hand-guessed macro set conflicts with wasi-libc decls and fails to compile. Lane B explicitly forbids any configure run, and hand-authoring a wasi-tuned config.h is precisely the per-tool host work the lanes prohibit (lanes-not-per-tool). No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (Lane A); it is C, not bare Rust/Python/JS (rules out C/D). The bundled lib/regex* is also redundant with already-live PCRE2/oniguruma. Verified: tarball HTTP 200; sed/*.c pulls 19 gnulib headers (xalloc, localcharset, acl, fwriting, unlocked-io, getopt, version-etc...); no flex/bison/yacc files (codegen not the blocker — the configure/gnulib coupling is).

name: J (jsoftware/jsource — J array language engine)
build_opts: n/a — not live-buildable

name: dhall (serde_dhall / dhall-rust)
blocker: Lane C disqualified on three independent grounds. (1) Proc-macros: deps pest_consume 1.1 + pest 2.1 — the parser is built via pest's proc-macro derive machinery; mrustc ~1.74 has no proc-macro expansion (still the pending frontier, not landed). (2) Build-time codegen: dhall/build.rs runs abnf_to_pest + pest_generator to convert src/syntax/text/dhall.abnf -> OUT_DIR/dhall.pest grammar during the build — a per-tool codegen step our lanes cannot run in-sandbox (same class as flex/bison/protoc). (3) Large multi-crate workspace (dhall + serde_dhall + abnf_to_pest + proc-macro helper), edition 2018, heavy generic/trait machinery (elsa, minicbor, once_cell, lazy_static) — well beyond a bare small crate. The 'pure total evaluator, ideal sandbox shape' observation is a RUNTIME property and does not bear on buildability; the build requires proc-macro expansion + ABNF->PEG codegen that the automated lanes cannot perform with no per-tool host work. Verified Cargo.toml + build.rs via gh api on master (crate 0.13.0).

blocker: Pure-JS Node CLI bundler (bin dist/cli.js, main dist/microbundle.js) — no .wasm, so lanes A/B/C are out. name: LLD (wasm-ld)
blocker: REDUNDANT with already-live LLVM tool. wasm-ld is not a separate buildable target — it is the WebAssembly flavor of LLVM lld, and in this repo it ships as part of the SAME llvm.core.wasm multitool that provides clang. It is prebuilt+sha-pinned (npm @yowasp/clang, YoWASP LLVM 22.1.0 built for wasm32-wasi), provisioned by runtime/compilers/clang/build.sh, and already invoked on every build path — C (clang/README.org L29), Zig (.zig→C→clang→wasm-ld, zig/README.org L8), and JS/QuickJS (js/build.sh L55-57: "wasm-ld qjs-run.wasm"). The clang lane IS the wasm-ld lane. Building or fetching wasm-ld separately yields no distinct value — it is already host-live as the LLVM tool listed in the redundancy exclusion set.

name: busybox
blocker: Two independent disqualifiers. (1) Configure/codegen: busybox builds via the Linux Kbuild/Kconfig system. `make defconfig` runs conf/mconf parsers generated from flex/bison lexers (scripts/kconfig/zconf.y, zconf.l), and the build compiles+RUNS host codegen tools — applets/applet_tables.c emits include/applet_tables.h, and scripts/gen_build_files.sh (sed/awk) emits include/applets.h / usage.h. These are per-tool configure + build-time exec codegen we cannot run in-sandbox; violates lanes-not-per-tool. A hand-written config header does not substitute for the applet_tables exec step. (2) Fundamental: busybox is a multicall binary whose core purpose is fork-exec of applets plus Linux process/syscall surface (mount, ps, raw sockets, /proc, tty/job control) — OS-process/syscall-as-core, which wasm32-wasi cannot provide; even a NOFORK subset depends on absent Linux syscalls. Also largely redundant with already-live coreutils/tar. Not live-buildable.

name: findutils
blocker: GNU findutils is an autotools+gnulib project that REQUIRES a ./configure run (generates config.h from hundreds of platform feature probes) plus gnulib bootstrap/codegen and per-tool source curation across find/ xargs/ locate/ gl/lib/ lib/ — this violates lane B (no configure, no codegen, no per-tool source-list curation). No verified plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists: wasmer.io/syrusakbary/findutils returns HTTP 404, npm 404. Not a Rust crate, not pure-Python/JS. Independently, xargs is fork-exec-as-purpose (spawns child processes) — a fundamental wasm32-wasi blocker. No clean automated lane.

name: 7-Zip (7z/p7zip)
smoke: N/A — not reachable via automated lanes.
blocker: Build requires per-tool source-list curation, which violates the lanes-not-per-tool rule. The Alone2 7zz target is defined by makefile.gcc that includes nested .mak fragments (7zip_gcc.mak, Format7zF/Arc_gcc.mak, var_*.mak) enumerating ~150 hand-picked object files via explicit O_* lists + per-directory vpath rules across deep trees (UI/Common, UI/Console, Compress/*, Crypto/*, Archive/*, C/, Common/, Windows/). It is NOT a flat src_globs+excludes set: a glob of CPP/7zip/** also pulls DLL/GUI/FAR-plugin/Windows-resource and p7zip-variant .cpp files that fail under wasm32-wasi, and the correct Alone2 file subset is selectively drawn from directories that also hold non-target sources. Replicating the makefile's curated object lists by hand = exactly the disqualified per-tool curation. (Positives that DON'T save it: pure C/C++, self-contained, no autotools/CMake configure run, no flex/bison/yacc/codegen, assembly is optional with pure-C fallbacks, and it ships its own MyWindows.h POSIX shim — but the curated source set is the hard blocker. -Werror default would also need stripping.)

blocker: xmlstarlet is a thin C CLI over libxml2 + libxslt + libexslt — a three-tarball stack where each project's build is driven by an autotools/CMake CONFIGURE run that generates feature-gated headers the source #ifdefs on: libxml2 produces config.h AND include/libxml/xmlversion.h + xmlexports.h (LIBXML_*_ENABLED matrix); libxslt adds config.h + xsltconfig.h + xsltexports.h tightly coupled to libxml2's macros; xmlstarlet itself is autotools (configure.ac/Makefile.am). Hand-writing a single small config header does not cover xmlversion.h/xsltconfig.h, which encode the build-time feature matrix the entire codebase branches on — that is per-tool source/config curation a configure run, not our lanes. No flex/bison but the configure-cascade across 3 projects is the lane-violating blocker. No confirmed prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (GitHub hits are Android/node-libxml/GH-action wrappers, none a wasi binary). XML-parse value also overlaps already-live expat and transform overlaps pandoc.

name: easy_install
blocker: easy_install is a pure-Python console script from setuptools/pkg_resources that simply rides CPython, which is already an ALREADY-LIVE tool (python). It is not a distinct buildable artifact: there is no C/C++/Rust/wasm to compile — it is just setuptools site-packages on top of the live Python interpreter. Per the triage rule, redundant-with-an-already-live-tool (python) with no distinct buildable value = impossible. Additionally easy_install's actual job is network package installation (fetch+install from PyPI), which is network-as-purpose / fork-exec of build steps — long-deprecated and a non-capability in-sandbox. No port needed; capability already covered by the live python lane.

name: composer
blocker: Composer is a pure-PHP phar, NOT a wasm artifact. It rides the already-LIVE php command (php-cgi-8.2.6.wasm, VMware WLR plain wasm32-wasi, sha-pinned in runtime/host/pallet.ex). Two disqualifiers: (1) redundant with an already-live tool (php) — no distinct buildable .wasm of its own; nothing to build via any lane. (2) Composer's defining function (install/update/require) is network-as-purpose: it resolves and downloads from repo.packagist.org over HTTPS, which the sandbox does not broker by default. Only trivial offline subcommands (--version/validate/dump-autoload) would parse, and even those are unverified given live php is CGI-SAPI not CLI (phar+argv pass-through unproven). Not live-buildable: there is no per-tool buildable artifact, and the product's purpose is the network.

name: ffmpeg
blocker: FFmpeg's build is gated on running ./configure, which is a per-tool host configure/codegen step our lanes can't run in-sandbox. configure generates config.h AND the component-registration source files that are NOT in the tree (libavcodec/codec_list.c, libavformat/protocol_list.c + muxer/demuxer lists, libavfilter/filter_list.c, bsf_list.c, parser_list.c) plus host-run table-generation tools (*_tablegen). This cannot be reduced to globs+excludes + a hand-written config header, so it fails Lane B's no-configure/no-codegen/no-source-curation constraints. Lane A: no confirmed plain prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm release exists — ffmpegwasm/ffmpeg.wasm is emscripten/JS-paired; the WASI repos (yanghaku, SebastiaanYN) ship build scripts/Dockerfiles that run configure+wasi-sdk, not a downloadable .wasm asset; the only registry artifact is Wasmer/WASIX, which our runtime deliberately does not adopt. Lanes C (Rust) and D (Python/JS) inapplicable — it is a large autotools-style C codebase.

name: qpdf

(The port_config.h.in is NOT a true configure blocker; it is auto-skipped via __has_include and only gates optional crc32c/snappy/zstd accel, so Lane B's config-header concern is moot.) Independently REDUNDANT: sqlite3 is already a live tool and covers the embedded persistent-storage / KV value with no distinct buildable advantage.

name: Oberon (OBNC)
blocker: OBNC is a build orchestrator, not a self-contained compiler. The top-level `obnc` driver (src/obnc.c) is fork/exec-as-core: it popen()s `obnc-compile` (the transpiler) and then system()s the host C compiler+linker to turn the emitted C into the final binary (src/obnc.c:179 popen, :281/:396/:695 system, :688 `cc -o ... ldLibs`). The README's own `dev-exec` branch narrative confirms it: they had to add a `Process.Execute` capability "to run any external process" / "call clang from there" precisely because the toolchain must shell out to a C compiler. That is fork-exec-as-purpose, which the sandbox cannot do. Secondary blockers: runtime dependency on Boehm GC (`LDLIBS=-lgc`, src/Util.env) and the GPL build script that re-runs lex/yacc when timestamps drift (lex.yy.c/y.tab.c ARE checked in, so codegen could be sidestepped, but the orchestration model is the disqualifier). Even the isolated obnc-compile transpiler only emits C text and produces no runnable artifact without the external toolchain — no distinct in-sandbox buildable value.

name: Nim

blocker: Two compounding blockers. (1) Bootstrap: the only way to get a `nim` binary is the csources_v2 pre-transpiled C, but those .nim.c files are generated per concrete OS/CPU (amd64/arm + linux/macos: posix.nim.c, os.nim.c, osproc.nim.c) — there is NO wasm32-wasi-targeted csources set, so clang.wasm+wasi-libc cannot "take over" the bootstrap; the generated C assumes a real POSIX platform and fork/exec/posix_spawn. (2) Build orchestration: even past bootstrap, getting the real compiler needs `koch boot` — a multi-stage process that re-invokes the freshly built `nim` to recompile itself (self-hosting fork-exec loop driven by build.sh/koch). (3) Core runtime: the `nim` driver's PURPOSE is to transpile to C then fork-exec an external C compiler (execvp gcc/clang via osproc) — fork-exec-as-core. The earlier "transpiles to portable C then our clang lane takes over" note conflated *running Nim output* with *building the Nim tool*; the tool itself is unbuildable and unrunnable in-sandbox (fork-exec-as-core + configure/koch orchestration), violating lanes-not-per-tool.

name: V (vlang)
blocker: V is a native-AOT codegen toolchain, not a droppable library. Verified: V's latest release (0.5.1) ships NO prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm asset (lane A out). V is distributed as bootstrap C (v.c amalgam + vlib/), but the v binary's core function is to transpile V source -> C and then fork-exec a backend C compiler (tcc/gcc/clang) to emit a native binary. That mechanism is native-AOT-codegen + fork-exec, both fundamental sandbox blockers. The pragmatic 'V -> C -> clang.wasm' path requires per-tool host orchestration (run V to emit C, then hand that C to our clang lane) which violates lanes-not-per-tool. The native/wasm backend is experimental/incomplete and not a usable library lane. Not lane B (it IS a codegen tool, not self-contained C library), not C/D.

name: Odin
blocker: Earlier "lane B live-likely" flag conflated Odin's BUILD TARGET (TargetMetrics target_wasi_wasm32 — Odin can EMIT wasm32-wasi output) with Odin THE COMPILER running in-sandbox. Those are orthogonal. The Odin compiler itself is a native C++ AOT-codegen tool whose backend is LLVM: it generates LLVM IR and links libLLVM to produce machine code. Compiling Odin to wasm32-wasi for our sandbox is not lane-reachable: (1) it requires building/linking LLVM, which needs a CMake configure run + tablegen IR/codegen — exactly the configure+codegen per-tool host work the lanes forbid; (2) it is native-AOT-codegen, a fundamental blocker class; (3) LLVM is already on the already-live/redundant list, so there is no distinct buildable value. No prebuilt plain (non-emscripten) wasm32-wasi .wasm of the Odin compiler exists. Not a self-contained clang+libc++ amalgam — large C++ tree with LLVM dependency.

name: Smalltalk
blocker: No plain wasm32-wasi Smalltalk VM exists. OpenSmalltalk-vm's only WASM target is Catalyst — a SqueakJS+WASM/WASM-GC browser hybrid that requires a JS host (excluded: emscripten/js-pair, not standalone wasi). Building the C VM from source is not lane-B reachable: it requires Slang (Smalltalk-to-C) codegen of the interpreter sources plus a CMake/autotools configure run and per-tool source curation around the image/plugin layout — all of which violate the no-configure/no-codegen/no-per-tool-curation rule. No bare mrustc-class Rust crate or pure-Python/JS Smalltalk exists. Fundamental host-coupling (JS host for the WASM path) + per-tool codegen blocker.

name: Modula-2
blocker: Only real M2 compiler is gm2 (a GCC front-end); GCC is native-AOT-codegen, does not emit wasm32-wasi, and requires a full autotools configure run plus bison/flex/m4 parser-generator codegen — all disallowed in-sandbox (lanes-not-per-tool). m2c (M2->C translator) likewise needs lex/yacc codegen. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (Lane A=no). Not a bare Rust crate / pure-Python / JS bundle (C/D=no).

name: yorick
blocker: Yorick ships a `configure` script that generates `Make.cfg` with platform-specific config (the play/ portability layer + yapi), so building it requires a per-tool configure run we cannot perform in-sandbox (violates lanes-not-per-tool). Beyond config: the play/ portability layer is built around a POSIX event loop (poll/select), terminal/tty I/O, and fork/exec subprocesses; gist/ wants X11. These are core to the interpreter's runtime (interactive REPL + event-driven I/O), not optional. Even though the parser is hand-written (no yacc/bison codegen) and the language core is plain ANSI C, you cannot reach a working `yorick` binary via our globs+excludes lane without (a) hand-authoring a Make.cfg-equivalent config header per platform AND (b) porting the play event-loop/fork-exec layer to wasm32-wasi. The prior lane-B note already concluded 'needs a port, not drop-in.' That makes it a per-tool host-work + fork-exec/event-loop blocker, not a clean lane-B amalgam.

name: XS (Moddable) — xst shell
blocker: Requires per-tool host porting that violates lanes-not-per-tool. Verified upstream (moddable@public): the ONLY wasm platform shipped is xs/platforms/wasm_xs.c, hard-coupled to emscripten.h + emscripten/html5.h (browser event loop) — i.e. the excluded emscripten/JS-pair target, not wasm32-wasi. No xs/makefiles/wasm/xst.mk exists (confirmed 404); wasm is wired only for the embedded `mc` simulator, never the standalone xst shell. xsPlatform.h gates wasm on #ifdef EMSCRIPTEN. The tool main xs/tools/xst.c uses native pthread_create (the test262 Atomics 'Agent' harness — native-threads-as-core), c_signal(SIGPIPE), and setjmp; the lin build links -ldl -lpthread -latomic. Although the source list itself is clean (flat fixed .c list across xs/sources + xs/tools + tools/fdlibm + tools/yaml + 3 modules dirs, NO configure run, NO flex/bison/yacc — hand-written xsLexical.c/xsSyntaxical.c lexer-parser, NO codegen), shipping wasm32-wasi would require hand-writing a brand-new WASI platform HAL to replace wasm_xs.c, stubbing the pthread agent harness in xst.c, and authoring a wasm makefile/source-list — bespoke per-tool host work, not a globs+excludes+config-header lane B fit.

name: porffor
build_opts: lane=D (JS-on-QuickJS bundle, NOT wasm32-wasi). entry=compiler/index.js (the compile API; do NOT use runtime/index.js — that's the Node CLI/REPL). pure-ESM, type=module. runtime deps: acorn (https://registry.npmjs.org/acorn/-/, pure JS, dist/acorn.mjs, zero deps, no gyp/install). node-repl-polyfill is REPL-only — exclude. Bundle: porffor compiler/*.js + builtins_precompiled.js (1.9M, SHIPPED in tarball, the precompiled stdlib — no codegen needed) + acorn into one qjs script. Shims: (1) parse.js L20 does import((globalThis.document?'https://esm.sh/':'')+parser) — no document in qjs → resolves bare 'acorn'; pre-bundle acorn so the dynamic import hits the bundled module. (2) fs/child_process/execSync are conditionally imported behind `typeof process?.version !== 'undefined'` and used ONLY for debug/disassemble/2c output — shim process={version:undefined, stdout:{write:print}} so the fs/execSync branches stay undefined and the pure compile path runs. API: default(source) -> {wasm: Uint8Array, exports, ...}; emit wasm bytes (assemble.js, pure-JS LEB128 via encoding.js, no Buffer/fs).
smoke: In qjs: load bundle, call porffor('export default () => 40 + 2') and assert the returned object has a non-empty wasm Uint8Array starting with the WASM magic (0x00 0x61 0x73 0x6d); optionally instantiate that wasm with our wasmtime/wasm host and call the export to get 42.
blocker: none for the compile-to-wasm-bytes path. Caveats (not blockers): set process.version=undefined so the node fs/child_process branches stay dormant — the -c (C output via 2c.js) and disassemble/debug paths assume Node and are out of scope; only the wasm-bytes path is in-scope. acorn dynamic import must be pre-resolved in the bundle.

name: Perl interpreter (perl)
blocker: No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (zeroperl has ZERO GitHub releases and no .wasm asset anywhere — verified via gh release list + code search). The only path is zeroperl's Docker pipeline, which runs Perl's own Configure (full autotools-style configure run producing config.h) AND bootstraps a native miniperl to generate Perl C sources/headers (host-native codegen), plus applies wasi patches and custom C stubs. That is per-tool configure+codegen we cannot run in-sandbox — exactly the lanes-not-per-tool violation. Cannot be reduced to clang+libc amalgam with a hand-written config header (Perl's config is deeply host/probe-derived; sources are generated by running miniperl). Not lane A (no wasm), not B (needs Configure+codegen), not C (C not Rust), not D.

name: WAMR (WebAssembly Micro Runtime) — classic/fast interpreter
blocker: WAMR is a wasm HOST runtime, not a wasm-targetable tool. core/config.h hard-requires a host BUILD_TARGET_* matching the CPU (x86_64/aarch64/arm/riscv/mips/xtensa/arc); __wasm32__ matches none -> #error "Build target isn't set". No emscripten/wasm32 branch in config.h or the platform layer anywhere. Platform abstraction (core/shared/platform/common/posix/) is native-POSIX: os_mmap uses MAP_ANONYMOUS|MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_JIT and mprotect (maps executable memory), plus sigaction/pthread_sigmask/pthread_kill/pthread for blocking-op + threads -- none available under baseline wasm32-wasi. So even the pure-C interpreter (invokeNative_general.c, no asm) cannot link. Building it would be wasm-in-wasm interpreting wasm, redundant with our already-live wasmtime engine and forbidden by the host-brokered isolation model. Not a config-header fix; it is a fundamental target/ABI mismatch (native mmap/mprotect/signals/threads as core).

name: Berkeley DB
blocker: Public API + internal headers are NOT shipped; they are produced by the autoconf configure run. configure.ac declares AC_CONFIG_HEADERS plus assembles db.h:src/dbinc/db.in (3085-line template, ~40 @type_decl@/@platform_header@/@db_seq_decl@ substitutions) + dbinc_auto/{api_flags,ext_def,ext_prot}.in, db_int.h:src/dbinc/db_int.in (@db_int_def@ = a configure-assembled typedef block, @DB_STRUCT_ALIGN8@, @PATH_SEPARATOR@), and db_config.h:config.hin (233 #undef HAVE_* feature-probe results). The clib/ and mutex/ source files are individually self-gated on HAVE_* macros (so they glob+self-exclude fine), and os_windows/os_vxworks/os_qnx/repmgr are excludable by dir — the source list is tractable. BUT the three required headers cannot be obtained without running configure: the @db_int_def@ typedef fragment and the 233 HAVE_* probe outcomes are configure-derived, not hand-writable constants. Reproducing them by hand = re-implementing the configure run per-tool, which violates the no-configure / lanes-not-per-tool rule. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (Lane A negative; only emscripten/sql.js-style experiments). Not Lane B because it needs a CONFIGURE run for header codegen, far beyond a small hand-written config header.

name: ag (The Silver Searcher)
blocker: Core value is pthread parallel search (native-threads-as-core); WASI lane has no native threads, leaving only a degraded single-threaded grep. Requires a configure run to generate config.h — source #ifdefs on 15+ HAVE_* probes (fopencookie/madvise/fgetln/strlcpy/posix_fadvise) plus BSD-only headers (sys/cpuset.h, sys/endian.h, pthread_np.h), so hand-writing the config header is per-tool source curation + WASI-libc feature guessing, not a clean glob compile. Links PCRE1 (#include <pcre.h>, deprecated) + zlib + lzma. Also redundant: regex already covered by live pcre2/onig. Confirmed against ggreer/the_silver_searcher 2.2.0 source (src/main.c worker-pool, configure.ac PKG_CHECK_MODULES libpcre/liblzma + AX_PTHREAD + AC_CHECK_FUNCS). Matches prior 'heavy fork, not a clean compile' note.

name: GraphicsMagick
blocker: GraphicsMagick is NOT a clean Lane B amalgam. (1) The coder layer (coders/*.c) is not a globbable source set: each format is conditionally compiled per configure-detected delegate lib, and the static module registration table (magick/static.c MagickModuleInit) is generated per-configure to list exactly which coders exist — requiring per-tool source-list curation + hand-edited registration beyond globs+excludes, which the lane forbids. (2) Its real value-add formats (PS/PDF/SVG/many) are implemented via fork/exec to external delegates (Ghostscript etc.) wired through delegates.mgk — fork/exec is a fundamental sandbox blocker. (3) The only subset that would actually compile (pure-C MagickCore pixel ops: resize/blur/composite/convert over raw RGBA plus built-in PNG/JPEG via libpng/libjpeg deps) is redundant with already-live png + jpeg + pixel-compute, so no distinct buildable value remains. magick_config.h being hand-writable does not rescue it — the coder codegen/curation and delegate fork-exec are the disqualifiers.

name: sharp / libvips
blocker: Lane A fails: the only prebuilt sharp wasm (@img/sharp-wasm32@0.35.1) is an emscripten+emnapi build, NOT plain wasm32-wasi. Verified: wasm imports come from minified emscripten module "a" (import "a" "b"...), the .node.js glue is emscripten Module bootstrap, and embedded strings show /emsdk/emscripten/... and emnapi/src/uv/threadpool.c (pthreads/uv). Requires emscripten JS glue + emnapi napi runtime — explicitly excluded by lane A. Lane B fails: sharp is a thin C++ shim over libvips, and libvips needs a meson configure+codegen run plus ~20 transitive native libs (versions.json: glib 2.89, libffi 3.5, aom, heif, tiff, mozjpeg, webp, lcms, expat, png, zlib-ng, highway, plus Rust resvg 0.47). glib and libvips both require autotools/meson configure + code generation, libffi needs per-arch FFI trampolines, resvg is Rust (large workspace, not bare crate), and the codec set assumes pkg-config wiring — all violate the no-configure/no-codegen/lanes-not-per-tool rule. Several codecs (png/expat/jpeg) are also already-live-redundant. Not C, not Rust-bare, not Python, not JS-on-QuickJS.

name: git
build_opts: deps: [libgit2 v1.7.2 tarball]. src_globs: src/libgit2/**/*.c, src/util/**/*.c, deps/xdiff/*.c, deps/llhttp/*.c, deps/pcre/*.c, deps/zlib/*.c. exclude: src/util/win32/**, src/libgit2/win32/**, src/util/hash/openssl.c, src/util/hash/mbedtls.c, src/util/hash/win32.c, src/util/hash/common_crypto.c, **/sha1dc/** (keep builtin sha via deps/zlib or src/util/hash/builtin.c — pick exactly one sha backend), src/cli/** (skip the CLI git binary first; build lib then add a single src/cli main). cflags: --target=wasm32-wasi --sysroot=$SYSROOT -DLIBGIT2_NO_FEATURES_H -DGIT_ARCH_32_or_64 -DGIT_THREADS=0 -DGIT_HTTPS=0 -DGIT_SSH=0 -DGIT_USE_NSEC=0 -DGIT_REGEX_BUILTIN=1 -DGIT_SHA1_BUILTIN=1 -DGIT_SHA256_BUILTIN=1 -DGIT_IO_POLL=0 -DGIT_IO_SELECT=0 -Isrc/util -Isrc/libgit2 -Iinclude -Ideps/xdiff -Ideps/llhttp -Ideps/pcre -Ideps/zlib -DNO_VIZ -DSTDC. extra_sources main: thin src/cli/cli.c (git CLI entrypoint) compiled last and linked against the lib objects. Hand-write include/git2_features.h-equivalent via -D set above (NO_FEATURES_H path); disable threads/tls/ssh/http-network features that need sockets.
smoke: echo files into a tmp dir; run: git init /tmp/r && git add . && git commit -m x && git log --oneline (local object/refs ops only — no network clone/fetch).
blocker: Network transports (clone/fetch/push over http/ssh) are unreachable in-sandbox: no sockets/TLS — those subcommands compile out (GIT_HTTPS=0/GIT_SSH=0). Threads disabled (GIT_THREADS=0). Must pick exactly ONE sha1/sha256 backend (builtin) and exclude the rest, and exclude all win32/ + openssl/mbedtls/commoncrypto hash sources or you get duplicate symbols / missing headers. The bundled CLI (src/cli) is secondary — build the library first, then a thin main; if CLI source-list proves fiddly, the libgit2 library itself is the live-buildable artifact.

name: ghostscript
blocker: No plain wasm32-wasi prebuilt exists: both wasm builds are emscripten/js-pair. jsscheller/ghostscript-wasm ships only an npm package built via emconfigure/emmake (arch_wasm.h emscripten arch header, MODULARIZE, EXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS, --pre-js/--post-js, no .wasm release asset); jerbob92 has no wasm release. Source build is not lane-B reachable: requires ./autogen.sh + ./configure (autoconf CONFIGURE run) plus --with-arch_h generated arch-detection header and genarch/echogs codegen + curated device list — per-tool configure/codegen we cannot run in-sandbox. Also relies on EMULATE_FUNCTION_POINTER_CASTS (function-pointer-cast UB), so only emscripten ports work; plain wasm32-wasi would trap.

The 113-file source set is also not a clean glob+exclude — splash/cairo/glib/qt backends and JPEG/PNG/TIFF/LCMS image writers are interleaved and selected by CMake option conditionals, so isolating the text-only subset for pdftotext is per-tool source-list curation. Both violate lanes-not-per-tool (no configure/codegen, no per-tool curation). Freetype is REQUIRED but is already-live, so that is not itself the blocker.

build_opts: Lane A prebuilt fetch — no build. asset: openssl.wasm (1,962,334 bytes, contentType application/wasm) from voltbuilder/openssl-wasm tag v1.1.1o. No sock_* imports (offline crypto CLI). Register as CommandRegistry entry running on wasmtime with args passthrough + preopened cwd. Pin URL by tag (v1.1.1o = OpenSSL 1.1.1o).

name: miller (mlr)
blocker: Pure-Go program (~99% Go, no C/Rust/Python/JS sources) — falls outside all four automated lanes. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists: release v6.18.1 ships only native-arch tarballs/deb/rpm (darwin/linux/freebsd/windows/aix), zero wasm asset. Our only Go-in-sandbox lane is go-yaegi (a Go INTERPRETER), not a GOOS=wasip1 Go compiler; yaegi cannot run a full real-world CLI with heavy stdlib/reflection/build-tags/embedded assets, and tinygo/native go-build was deliberately dropped. Reaching it would require standing up a real Go-to-wasm compiler = per-tool host work, which violates lanes-not-per-tool. (Compounded: Miller's DSL parser is GOCC-generated codegen.)

name: librsvg (rsvg-convert)
blocker: librsvg is a large Rust workspace (now Rust core: cairo-rs/pango/gdk-pixbuf/glib gobject bindings + markup5ever/selectors proc-macro derives, edition 2021+, build-script codegen) — fails lane C (mrustc ~1.74 bare-crate-only, no proc-macros/workspace). The rendering stack (cairo, pango, fontconfig, GLib/GObject, gdk-pixbuf) is C requiring meson/autotools configure runs + glib-mkenums/gobject codegen per dep — violates lanes-not-per-tool (B forbids configure+codegen). No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi rsvg-convert .wasm exists (only emscripten/js demos). Multiple fundamental blockers; not reachable via any automated lane.

name: pango
blocker: Pango is built on GLib/GObject and uses Meson exclusively. Reaching it requires per-tool host work our lanes forbid: GLib needs a Meson configure run (generated config.h probing platform features) plus codegen tools (glib-genmarshal, glib-mkenums, gobject-introspection); FontConfig and Cairo likewise need configure runs. No plain glob-buildable source list exists (Meson-only, generated headers). It also leans on HarfBuzz + FreeType which are already-live tools, making the shaping/raster value redundant; Pango's distinct bidi/itemization/line-breaking layer cannot be isolated without the GLib configure+codegen chain. Violates lanes-not-per-tool (configure + codegen) and partially redundant with live harfbuzz/freetype.

name: BoringSSL

NO -DBORINGSSL_FIPS (avoids sys/mman.h/mprotect in bcm.cc). cflags: -DOPENSSL_NO_ASM -std=c++17 -fno-exceptions. entropy: falls through target.h __wasm32__ -> OPENSSL_RAND_GETENTROPY (WASI random_get). No configure, no codegen run, no flex/bison/protoc.

blocker: None blocking. Notes: must define OPENSSL_NO_ASM (skip all gen/bcm,gen/crypto .S/.asm); must build non-FIPS (BORINGSSL_FIPS guards the only sys/mman.h+mprotect use in bcm.cc); single-threaded wasi-libc fine (locks are no-ops). All codegen (perlasm .S, err_data.cc) and config (opensslconf.h) are COMMITTED in gen/ + include/ — confirmed no pregenerate/configure/codegen step needed. Distinct value vs live mbedtls/libsodium: full OpenSSL-compatible libcrypto+libssl TLS/X.509 API surface.

name: LibreSSL
build_opts: n/a — not reachable by globs+excludes+one config header
smoke: n/a
blocker: Verified against libressl-portable 4.3.2 tarball. NOT lane-B-clean: (1) crypto build is a 700-line curated CRYPTO_SRC list with per-arch conditionals; a glob over crypto/**/*.c pulls conflicting arch-companion C (bn/arch/amd64/*.c, aes/aes_amd64.c, *_aarch64.c/_amd64.c, every arch's crypto_cpu_caps.c) that duplicate symbols and reference asm — excludes can't substitute because the build REQUIRES exactly one crypto/arch/<arch>/{crypto_arch.c,crypto_arch.h} + one bn/arch/<arch>/ subtree, and NO wasm32 arch exists (only amd64/aarch64/riscv64/mips/ppc/sparc/loongarch). You'd have to author a brand-new wasm32 arch port (new crypto_arch.h, bn_arch.h, cpu_caps stub), not hand-write a single config header. (2) The portable compat layer keys off ~40 HAVE_* macros that configure derives via compile/link feature-tests against the target libc; wasi-libc has a non-obvious subset (no arc4random_buf/getauxval/syslog, getentropy/explicit_bzero/poll/endian-header quirks) — matching them is per-tool host configure work, not globs. (3) RNG (crypto/compat/getentropy_*.c) is OS-specific and needs a real wasm32-wasi getentropy port. This violates lanes-not-per-tool (needs a configure run or equivalent per-tool source/macro curation). Also redundant: mbedtls is already live and covers the TLS/crypto primitive need.

name: Idris2
blocker: Self-hosted compiler: bootstrapping Idris2 requires an existing Idris2 binary OR compiling its emitted Chez Scheme via Chez Scheme — an external bootstrap toolchain we cannot run in-sandbox. The codebase is Idris2 (not C/C++/Rust/Python/JS), so lanes A-D do not apply: no prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (lane A fails); the only C/C++ in the repo is the RTS support, not the compiler (lane B fails); not Rust (C); not a runnable pure-Python or QuickJS bundle without first bootstrapping (D). This is a native-AOT-codegen + self-hosting-bootstrap fundamental blocker.

name: ATS
blocker: ATS2/Postiats is a self-hosted compiler: 180k+ LOC written in ATS1, bootstrapped from pre-generated C. Building it requires an autotools ./configure run plus ATSLIB prelude/libats setup and PATSHOME env wiring — not a self-contained C amalgam buildable with globs+excludes. The configure-run requirement violates lane B (no configure/codegen permitted). No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (no Lane A; only Rust/C wasi targets surface, confirmed prior). Not a bare Rust crate (no Lane C), not pure-Python/JS (no Lane D). No automated capability-lane reaches it without per-tool host configure work.

name: Hermes
blocker: Hermes (Facebook's JS engine) requires a full CMake configure run plus codegen that we cannot perform in-sandbox: it generates Unicode tables (genUnicode Python scripts -> .inc files), generated parser/lexer support, and feature-detection headers, and relies on a curated LLVM-derived ADT/Support subset (hundreds of files) whose source list is driven by CMake target definitions — not expressible as globs+excludes. This is per-tool host configure/codegen, which the lanes forbid. It is also a JS engine, redundant with the already-live QuickJS (qjs) lane, with no distinct buildable value reachable automatically. No confirmed prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (only emscripten/asm.js artifacts ship from Hermes). Disabling the JIT yields an interpreter but does not remove the CMake+codegen barrier.

name: Helm
blocker: Helm is written in Go. Our automated capability-lanes are A (prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm), B (self-contained C/C++ via clang+libc++), C (bare Rust via mrustc), D (pure-Python pip / JS-on-QuickJS). None covers Go: no Go compiler in-sandbox, and Go needs native AOT codegen which is an explicit fundamental blocker. No confirmed prebuilt plain (non-js) wasm32-wasi helm binary is published — Helm's only wasm path is a user-built GOOS=wasip1 module, which still requires the Go toolchain we can't run. The full helm binary also relies on kube API networking and plugin fork-exec as core. Even the render-only 'helm template' subset is unreachable because the language lane itself is absent.

name: GHC RTS (Haskell)
blocker: No standalone wasm32-wasi RTS artifact exists. GHC's wasm support ships ONLY as a full cross-compiler toolchain (ghc-wasm-meta nix flake / bootstrap.sh installing wasm32-wasi-ghc to ~/.ghc-wasm). The RTS is hand-written C+Cmm built as part of the GHC build via Hadrian/Cabal + autotools configure, with Cmm files compiled by GHC's own native-AOT backend (not clang). It is shipped as .a archives linked at GHC-link time, never a usable standalone .wasm. None of our lanes apply: not a fetchable plain wasm (A), not self-contained clang+libc++ buildable without configure/codegen — it needs the full GHC build system + configure + Cmm codegen (violates lanes-not-per-tool, fails B), not Rust (C), not Python/JS (D). Fundamental blocker: native-AOT-codegen toolchain requiring per-tool configure + a bespoke compiler backend.

name: GnuTLS
blocker: Multi-dep autotools-configure + codegen cascade, and redundant with live crypto. (1) GnuTLS core requires an autotools `configure` run to generate config.h plus headers from .in templates (version/ABI/symbol logic) and uses gperf/codegen — we cannot run configure in-sandbox. (2) Hard deps GMP (bignum: configure-selected arch-specific mpn asm, not an amalgam) and nettle/hogweed (own autotools configure) are each per-tool configure jobs — violates lanes-not-per-tool. (3) ASN.1 via libtasn1 ships a generated parser. (4) TLS/crypto value is already covered by ALREADY-LIVE mbedtls + libsodium, so no distinct buildable value. Not Lane B (needs configure + codegen on itself and on 2+ deps); not A/C/D.
